A single MetricFlow query can't produce this count directly. All `where` filters are ANDed on the same exploded row, so a row can't be both `fig-007579` and `48336`. Metric-in-filter subqueries also can't take their own item filter, and no metric counts distinct items across part and minifig kinds. The closest single query lists, for each set, which of the two items it contains (part 48336 in all colours combined):

```json
{"metrics": ["where_used_count"], "group_by": ["set", "item"], "where": ["{{ Entity('item') }} IN ('fig-007579', '48336')"], "order_by": ["set", "item"]}
```

The answer is the number of distinct `set` values that appear in two rows, one for each item. Counting those needs a step outside MetricFlow, such as a SQL `HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT item) = 2` or a post-processing step on the result.

```json
{"metrics": ["catalog_minifigs", "catalog_parts"], "group_by": ["set"], "where": ["{{ Entity('item') }} IN ('fig-000506', '98138')"], "order_by": ["set"]}
```

This query cannot return the count as a single number. MetricFlow applies `where` filters per row and has no HAVING, so one query cannot require a set to contain both items. Instead, it returns one row per set that contains either item. `catalog_minifigs` is the quantity of fig-000506 and `catalog_parts` is the quantity of 98138, both at any depth in the current inventory. The answer is the number of rows where both columns are non-null and greater than 0.

A single MetricFlow query can't directly intersect two items. Each `where` filter applies per exploded row, and no governed metric counts distinct minifigs and parts together per set. The closest query lists every set containing either item, with one row per set and item pair.

```json
{"metrics": ["where_used"], "group_by": ["set", "item"], "where": ["{{ Entity('item') }} IN ('fig-003310', '88646')"], "order_by": ["set", "item"]}
```

The answer is the number of distinct `set` codes that appear in two rows, one for `fig-003310` and one for `88646`. This query does not return that count as a single value.
